:Judgment:

This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the injuries sustained in the Road Traffic accident.

2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 08.06.2019 at about 11.30 a.m., the Petitioner was standing on the extreme left side of the road in order to cross the road by observing the vehicles on the road near Peenya Industrial area, 2nd cross, near Kurlan factory, Bangalore, at that time,
the driver of car bearing KA-04-MT-8213 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner.
Due to the impact, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately, after the accident, the Petitioner was shifted to Med Star hospital, wherein he was treated as an inpatient.
Prior to the accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy and he was working in a bakery and was earning a sum of Rs.15,000/-p.m.
Due to the accident, he has sustained grievous injuries causing permanent disablement.

The Respondent No.1 is the owner of the offending vehicle and the Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle and therefore, both Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner.
Hence, this Petition.
3. Upon service of notice, the Respondent No.1 and 2 appeared through their respective counsels and filed separate objections to the main petition.

Respondent No.1 in his objection Statement denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending car.

Further he contended that there was traffic jam at the place of accident at time of accident,
hence he was moving slowly.
The accident was caused solely due to negligence of the petitioner who suddenly came running on the road and he himself dashed the car and not due to the negligence on the part of driver of the car.

On these grounds, Respondent No.1 has prayed to dismiss the petition against him.
4. Respondent No.2 in its objection Statement denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending car.

Further it contended that the accident was caused solely due to negligence of the petitioner himself who was crossing the road without observing the traffic and not due to the negligence on the part of driver of the car.
Further contended that owner of the insured car has not intimated the alleged accident to this respondent and there is violation of Section 134 of Motor Vehicles Act.

Further it contended that the driver of the vehicle was not possessing valid and effective driving license to drive the vehicle and the owner of the car entrusted the vehicle to a person who was not having valid driving licence.
On these grounds, Respondent No.2 has prayed to Manoj H.K vs Vijay Vittal.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings, my learned predecessor has framed the following Issues.
ISSUES 1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that he sustained grievous injuries in the nature of permanent disablement on 08.06.2019 at about 11.30 a.m., Peenya Industrial area, 2nd cross, near Kurlan factory, Bengaluru, in an accident arising due to rash and negligent driving of driver of car bearing KA-04-MT-8213?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation? If so, how much and from whom?

3. What Order or Award?
6.
In order to substantiate the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 6 documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.6.
He also got examined doctor as P.W.2 and got marked documents as per Ex.P-7 and 8 and closed his side evidence.
On the other hand, the Respondents have not adduced any evidence.

7. Having heard the arguments of the learned Counsel for the Petitioner and the learned Counsel for the Respondent No.2 upon perusal of the depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on record, my answer to the above Issues are as under:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No. 2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No. 3 : As per the Final Order  for the following :
 REASONS 8. Issue No. 1 : It is the case of the Petitioner that he had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic accident that occurred on 08.06.2019 at about 11.30 a.m., due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of car bearing KA-04-MT- 8213 by its rider.
9.
On the other hand, the Respondents have denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of car bearing KA-04-MT-8213 by its driver.
10. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, he got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 6 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P-6.
P.W.1 has re-iterated the Petition averments in her chief-affidavit.
Ex . P-1
to Ex.P-6 are the true copies of FIR along with complaint, spot panchanama along with sketch, IMV report, wound certificate and charge sheet.
Ex.P.6 is notarised copy of aadhar card.

3 11.

Upon going through Ex.P-1 FIR along with Complaint, same is evident that on the complaint lodged before Peenya Traffic Police station, the concerned Police have registered the case against the driver of car bearing KA-04-MT-8213 for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337 of IPC.

The charge sheet marked at Ex.P.5 discloses the fact that after thorough investigation IO has charge sheeted the driver of car bearing KA-04-MT-8213 for the offences punishable under Secs.279, 338 of IPC.
Ex.P.2 is the copy of Spot panchanama along with sketch justifies that same is drawn in the presence of panchas, The Ex

.P.3 the copy of IMV report justify the fact of involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident and the said document also discloses that the cause of accident was not due to any mechanical defects of the vehicle involved in question.
The Ex.P.4 the copy of wound certificate discloses that as a result of RTA the petitioner sustained grievous and simple injuries.
Ex.P.4 is the copy of wound certificate, which discloses that petitioner has sustained grievous injuries due to road traffic accident.

The document Ex.P.5 is the copy of Charge sheet shows that after thorough investigation, the PSI of Peenya Traffic Police Station has Charge-sheeted the driver of the offending car for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 338 of IPC.
12. PW1 is subjected for cross examination by the learned counsel for Respondent No.1 and 2.
During his cross examination he has denied that there is no negligence on the part of the driver of the offending car.
13. Moreover, the charge sheet is the material document, which is not challenged by the driver of the offending vehicle.

Therefore, having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and evidence adduced by the Petitioner and the documents exhibited, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, the Petitioner has proved that the said accident has occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of car bearing KA-04-MT-8213 and in the said accident, the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 is in the "Affirmative".
14. Issue No

. 2 : As the petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of car bearing KA-04-MT-8213 by its driver, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.
15. In the petition, the Petitioner has shown his age as 19 years.
He has produced Aadhar card at Ex.P.6 to prove his age.
As per the Aadhar card, the date of birth of the petitioner is shown as 04.05.2000.
The accident has taken place on 08.06.2019.

Hence, the age of the Petitioner, as on the date of accident was taken as 19 years and the same is to be taken for consideration.
16.
Further, the petitioner has averred that he was working in a bakery and earning a sum of Rs.15,000/-p.m.
In this regard, he has not produced any documents to prove his avocation.
Therefore, in the absence of any income proof, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, the notional income to be assessed as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority.
Since the accident has been occurred in the year 2019, the notional income of Rs.14,000/- p.m. taken for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
17. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioner is entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :

I COMPENSATION TOWARDS PAIN, SHOCK AND SUFFERING:
18. It is to be noted here that according to the petitioner, he has sustained grievous injuries.
Ex. P.4

Wound certificate shows that the Petitioner had sustained following injuries:
1. Swelling over left leg.
X-ray shows Fracture shaft of tibia - left Fracture shaft of fibula - left.
As per the Wound Certificate, the doctor has opined that injury No.1 is grievous in nature.
Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.30,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.

II COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF AMENITIES :
19.
The petitioner admitted to the hospital for the injuries sustained by him.
Bearing in mind the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.

III COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID -UP PERIOD:
20.
The Petitioner has averred in the petition as well as in his evidence that he was admitted as an inpatient from 08.06.2019 and discharged on 13.06.2019 at Med Star hospital.
But in this regard no evidence is adduced, in fact discharge summery also not produced.
However, the wound certificate proves that he sustained fracture of both bones.
Even the PW.2 doctor also deposed that as per recent X-ray which is marked at Ex.P.8 fractures are united with implant in-situ.
So it clarifies that he sustained fractures and it took minimum one month for healing.
Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that the laid up period may be considered as one month.

Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.14,000/- under this head (@
Rs.14,000/- per month).

IV COMPENSATION TOWARDS ATTENDANT'S CHARGES, EXTRA DIET & NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE :
21.

Admittedly, the Petitioner has sustained injuries and during the laid up period, the Petitioner might have engaged an attendant and also he might have spent some amount towards extra diet and nourishment and for his conveyance.

In the facts and circumstances of the case, awarding compensation of Rs.6,000/- towards attendants charges, Rs.6,000/- towards extra diet and nourishment and Rs.6,000/- towards conveyance would be just and reasonable.
In all, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.18,000/- under this head.
V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENSES :

sentences.text: The Petitioner has deposed that he has spent more than Rs.5,00,000/- towards medical expenses.
However, the petitioner has not produced any medical bills.
Such being the case, this Tribunal is of the view that the petitioner is not entitled to any compensation under this head.

VI COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS/COMPENSATION TOWARDS PERMANENT DISABILITY :
23.

The Petitioner has alleged that due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident, he has suffered permanent disablement and due to the injury he is getting head ache and giddiness often,
cannot walk, stand, sit squat on the floor, cannot use Indian type toilet, cannot lift or carry weight.
Even in his evidence, P.W.1 has deposed to that effect.
24. Further, the Petitioner got examined doctor by name Dr.Nagaraj.B.N as P.W.2 who also deposed regarding the injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.
He further deposed that petitioner had sustained left leg both bones fracture.
He assessed physical disability of 42% left lower limb and whole body disability at 14%.
25. In the cross-examination PW.2 has stated that he has not personally treated the petitioner.
He has admitted that after lapse of two years petitioner approached him for assessment of disability.
He has admitted that petitioner has not furnished any follow up records.
In his examination chief itself he deposed that the fractures are united.

26. Hence, having regard to the medical records placed on hand and the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner keeping in mind the age of the petitioner and by considering the nature of his work, upon consideration of the fact that the petitioner got examined himself before this court as PW.1 and in the absence of the discharge summery and case sheet, Tribunal is of the view that the disability assessed appears to be at the higher rate.

Hence, having regard to the evidence placed on record and the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner and by considering the age, I am of the opinion that considering the disability of the Petitioner with respect to the whole body at 10%
would be just and proper.
27. As per Sarla Verma's Case (2009 ACJ 1298 SC), the multiplier applicable to the age of Petitioner is 18.

With multiplier of 18, income of Rs.14,000/- per month and disability of the Petitioner with respect to his whole body at 10%, the loss of future income comes to Rs.3,02,400/-
(Rs.14,000x12x18x10% =3,02,400 /-).
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,02,400/- under this head.

TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
28.

To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1. Pain, shock & Suffering Rs. 30,000/-

Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.3,84,400/- with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.

29. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending car bearing KA-04-MT-8213.

There is no dispute of the fact that the respondent No.1 is the owner and the respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending car are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation amount to the petitioner.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "Partly in the Affirmative".
30. ISSUE No. 3 :

In view of my findings on Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the U/Sec. 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner is entitled for Compensation of Rs.3,84,400/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.

The Respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.
